summary: Both sides are a 13-entry 'real world light source' selector with matching hue families and matching animated/static mode positions, but the port's three flickering modes are continuously-modulated, spatially-coherent and ~2x too bright instead of the original's sparse independent per-pixel flares, mode 10 is a 5-px repeating pattern instead of a flat violet, and the slider->mode mapping is /13 instead of /12 so half the dial range selects a different light type.
observations: Rig: 1D strip, 60 px. Both sides compile and run clean (no compileError/runtimeError), neither binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both). Control surface MATCHES exactly: one `slider` named `sliderLightType` (label 'LightType') on each side.

Untouched defaults land on mode 0 on both sides (orig meanR/G/B 92.5/24.5/1, meanBrightness 39.4; port 132.1/37.3/0, meanBrightness 56.5 over the 6 s baseline) — the untouched divergence is exactly the mode-0 divergence described below, not a separate default-state bug.

MODE STRUCTURE: a 41-point dial sweep (v = 0.000..1.000 step 0.025, 2 s @20 fps each, frames hashed) shows BOTH sides expose 13 discrete light types in the SAME order with the SAME three animated ones (indices 0, 4, 12) and ten static ones. Per-mode strip colour (mean R/G/B, orig vs port): 0 flicker amber 91/24/1 vs 132/37/0; 1 255/127/35 vs 255/177/109; 2 255/170/98 vs 255/205/166; 3 255/238/245 vs 255/254/250; 4 flicker green 27/69/0 vs 57/129/0; 5 255/67/7 vs 255/68/0; 6 140/255/147 vs 198/255/228; 7 255/135/24 vs 255/114/0; 8 255/203/203 vs 255/221/209; 9 211/235/255 vs 216/237/255; 10 100/0/255 vs (non-uniform, see below); 11 167/0/255 vs 173/0/255; 12 flicker blue 0/30/67 vs 0/52/129.

SLIDER->MODE MAPPING DIFFERS. Measured boundary positions: orig switches at multiples of 1/12 (0.0833, 0.1667, 0.25, 0.3333, 0.4167, 0.5, 0.5833, 0.6667, 0.75, 0.8333, 0.9167) — i.e. index = floor(v*12), so its 13th light type (mode 12, dark blue) is reachable ONLY at exactly v = 1.0 (verified: v = 0.99 / 0.999 / 0.9999 all give mode 11's 167,0,255; v = 1.0 gives 0,23,50). Port switches at multiples of 1/13 (0.0769, 0.1538, 0.2308, 0.3077, 0.3846, 0.4615, 0.5385, 0.6154, 0.6923, 0.7692, 0.8462, 0.9231) — index = floor(v*13), so mode 12 owns the whole top 1/13 of the range. Consequence: floor(12v) != floor(13v) over exactly HALF of [0,1], so half of all slider positions select a DIFFERENT light type on the two sides (e.g. v = 0.325 -> orig mode 3 near-white, port mode 4 dark green; v = 0.80 -> orig mode 9 cool white 211/235/255, port mode 10).

MODE 0 (default, candle/fire) FLICKER CHARACTER IS THE BIG DIVERGENCE. 200 frames dumped at 0.05 s spacing, 20 fps: both sides share the SAME resting ember colour (R = 89, G = 24-25, B = 0-1). Original: only 13.6% of pixel-samples sit more than 3 counts above that baseline; median R across the whole window is exactly 89 (p50 89, p75 89, p95 130, p99 179, max 217); ~18-25 of 60 pixels change per frame with a mean delta of only ~2 counts. Port: 76.6% of samples are above baseline (p25 95, p50 127, p75 159, p95 202, max 254); 49-60 of 60 pixels change EVERY frame with mean delta 5-10 counts. In words: the original is a calm dark ember with occasional gentle flares, the port is a permanently busy shimmering strip.

MODE 0 FLARE SHAPE AND RATE. Single-pixel trace (px 16, R channel, 20 fps): original rests at flat 89 for ~38 frames, then a smooth symmetric flare 89 -> 152 -> 89 lasting ~22 frames (1.1 s), then rest again — about 0.3 flares/s/pixel, ~14% duty. Port's same pixel never returns to a long rest: 89 for 13 frames, flare to 134, only dips to 94, immediately flares to 204, brief 8-frame rest, flares to 167, etc. Port flares are both ~35% taller and roughly 5x more frequent, and they overlap.

MODE 0 SPATIAL COHERENCE. Correlation of each pixel's time series against its neighbours' over the 10 s dump: original |corr| <= 0.17 at every spatial lag 1..16 (pixels flicker INDEPENDENTLY — the waterfall is scattered isolated dashes on a flat base). Port shows strong deterministic structure: lag 1 = -0.37, lag 5 = -0.40, lag 6 = +0.51, lag 10 = +0.48, lag 11 = -0.71 — adjacent pixels anti-correlated with a repeating spatial motif, which is what produces the port's dense diagonal/checkerboard waterfall texture.

MODE 0 GLOBAL PULSATION. Autocorrelation of the whole-strip mean R (raw series, lag scan in frames at 20 fps): original decays monotonically 0.98 -> 0.13 over 3 s with NO negative lobe (aperiodic). Port swings to -0.95 at lag 9 (0.45 s) and back to +0.90 at lag 18 (0.90 s) — the port's whole strip breathes together with a ~0.9 s period. The original strip has no whole-strip rhythm at all.

MODE 4 (dark green) SAME PATTERN OF ERROR. Original: G baseline 63, p50 = 63 (at rest most of the time), p95 114, max 180, motion.avg 0.0 / motionLit 0.2, zeroMotionFrames 120/120 over 6 s — visually near-static with rare slow swells; strip-mean autocorr decays monotonically with no oscillation. Port: G baseline 63 but p50 = 127, p95 202, max 251, motion.avg 1.0, zeroMotionFrames 2/120, and strip-mean autocorr reaches -0.87 at lag 27 (period ~2.7 s) — a continuous global oscillation. Port mean brightness 61.5 vs orig 32.2 (1.9x).

MODE 12 (dark blue, the v=1.0 mode) SAME PATTERN. Original: B baseline 50, p50 = 50, p95 150, max 245, meanBrightness 32.2, zeroMotionFrames 66/120 — sparse flares against a flat dark base, with a weak ~1.8 s rhythm (strip-mean autocorr -0.67 at lag 17-18, +0.57 at lag 36-37). Port: B p50 = 127, p95 201, max 252, meanBrightness 59.6 (1.85x), zeroMotionFrames 1/120, and a slow non-repeating swell (autocorr decays monotonically to 0 over ~1.4 s, no negative lobe) — so the port both over-drives this mode and drops the original's ~1.8 s cadence.

MODE 10 IS STRUCTURALLY WRONG. At v = 0.8397 (mode 10 on BOTH mappings) the original renders a flat uniform violet — every pixel 100,0,255 or 99,0,255 (a +-1 dither), spread [1,0,0], motion 0, static over the whole window. The port renders a 5-PIXEL REPEATING SPATIAL PATTERN: [0,71,255] [60,0,255] [255,0,235] [255,0,235] [60,0,255] repeated 12 times down the strip (azure / violet / magenta / magenta / violet), spread [255,71,21]. No original mode anywhere in the 13 has spatial structure like this, so this is invented, not a mis-indexed match.

STATIC MODE COLOUR ACCURACY (exact dumped RGB, uniform across the strip on both sides). Near-exact: mode 5 (255,67,7 vs 255,68,0), mode 9 (211,235,255 vs 216,237,255), mode 11 (167,0,255 vs 173,0,255), mode 3 (255,238,245 vs 255,254,250), mode 8 (255,203,203 vs 255,221,209). Noticeably DESATURATED on the port: mode 1 (255,127,35 vs 255,177,109 — G +50, B +74), mode 2 (255,170,98 vs 255,205,166 — G +35, B +68), mode 6 (140,255,147 vs 198,255,228 — R +58, B +81). Slightly off in the other direction: mode 7 (255,135,24 vs 255,114,0 — port redder/darker). The consistent sign is that the port's warm/tinted whites are pulled toward neutral white.

BOTH SIDES ARE TIME-BASED, NOT FRAME-COUPLED. Rendering mode 0 at 10, 20 and 40 fps and dumping the same absolute times gives essentially identical pixel values on each side at each time (orig px0-5 at t=0: 89,89,89,89,98,89 at all three rates; port px0-5 at t=1.0: 163/90/97/156/125/136 @10 fps vs 165/98/99/142/138/133 @20 fps vs 165/102/100/134/144/132 @40 fps — small integration-step drift only). motion.avg scales inversely with fps on both sides as expected. No frame-rate coupling finding on either side.

BOTH SIDES ARE SEED-INDEPENDENT. Seeds 1, 7 and 1234 (20 s @10 fps, mode 0) give byte-identical summary stats on both sides (orig mean 42 motion 1; port mean 56 motion 5), consistent with the smooth deterministic flare shapes — this pattern is not RNG-driven on either side, so per-pixel comparison is legitimate here.

STEADY STATE IS FINE ON BOTH. 240 s survey @5 fps: orig mean 41 motion 2, port mean 56 motion 9, both brightnessTrend steady, no regime change or new mode anywhere in the window. Late window (--skip 240, 30 s @10 fps): orig meanBrightness 41.2 (min 38 max 45) motion 1.2 zeroMotionFrames 52/300 steady; port 56.4 (min 55 max 59) motion 4.5 zeroMotionFrames 0/300 steady. Neither side dies, decays, or saturates. A static mode (mode 2) held EXACTLY 255/170/98 (orig) and 255/205/166 (port) for a full 180 s with zeroMotionFrames 360/360 on both — the static modes are genuinely static, not slowly drifting.

Overall brightness bias: the port is 1.43x brighter than the original in mode 0 (56.5 vs 39.4), 1.91x in mode 4 (61.5 vs 32.2) and 1.85x in mode 12 (59.6 vs 32.2) — the gap is concentrated in the three ANIMATED modes and comes from the flicker sitting near mid-scale instead of resting at baseline, not from a different base colour (the baselines match).

dials.name: sliderLightType
dials.origEffect: Mode selector, index = floor(v*12) -> 13 light types. Snaps the whole strip between distinct looks at v multiples of 1/12: 0 flickering amber ember (default), 1 warm orange 255/127/35, 2 warm white 255/170/98, 3 near-white 255/238/245, 4 dim flickering green 27/69/0, 5 red-orange 255/67/7, 6 pale green 140/255/147, 7 orange 255/135/24, 8 pink-white 255/203/203, 9 cool blue-white 211/235/255, 10 flat violet 100/0/255, 11 purple 167/0/255, 12 (ONLY at exactly v=1.0) dim flickering blue 0/23/50. Probe maxDelta 141.74.
dials.portEffect: Same 13 light types in the same order and the same three animated slots, but index = floor(v*13), so every boundary sits at a multiple of 1/13 and mode 12 occupies the whole top 1/13 of the range instead of the single point v=1.0. Net: half of all slider positions select a different light type than the original does. Within-mode colours mostly track (modes 3,5,8,9,11 near-exact) but modes 1,2,6 are markedly desaturated, mode 7 is redder, mode 10 is a 5-px repeating azure/violet/magenta pattern instead of flat violet, and modes 0/4/12 flicker far too hard. Probe maxDelta 171.30.

feedback: Mode-index mapping: the port divides the slider into 13 equal bands (floor(v*13)); the original divides it into 12 (floor(v*12)) with the 13th light type reachable only at exactly slider = 1.0. Measured boundaries — orig 0.0833/0.1667/0.25/0.3333/0.4167/0.5/0.5833/0.6667/0.75/0.8333/0.9167, port 0.0769/0.1538/0.2308/0.3077/0.3846/0.4615/0.5385/0.6154/0.6923/0.7692/0.8462/0.9231. Because floor(12v) != floor(13v) over half of [0,1], half the dial currently shows the wrong light. Match the /12 mapping.

Mode 0 (the default flickering ember) is the headline fix. The original rests at a flat baseline (R=89, G=24, B=1) with the median pixel EXACTLY at baseline and only ~14% of pixel-samples lit above it; the port sits at a median R of 127 with 77% of samples above baseline. Cut the flicker duty cycle by roughly 5x so the strip is mostly at rest, and cap the flare peak nearer 150-180 rather than 200-255. Target strip meanBrightness ~39 on 60 px, not ~57.

Mode 0 flare envelope: the original's flare is a single smooth symmetric rise-and-fall from baseline to peak and back over ~1.1 s (about 22 frames at 20 fps) at a rate of roughly one flare per pixel per 3 s, with the pixel pinned at baseline in between. The port's flares run back to back and only partially decay before the next one starts.

Mode 0 spatial independence: the original's pixels flicker INDEPENDENTLY (neighbour time-series correlation |r| <= 0.17 at every spatial lag 1..16), so its waterfall is scattered isolated dashes. The port's neighbours are deterministically locked (lag1 r = -0.37, lag6 +0.51, lag11 -0.71), producing a dense diagonal/checkerboard texture and a whole-strip pulse with a ~0.9 s period (strip-mean autocorr -0.95 at 0.45 s). The original has NO whole-strip rhythm — drive each pixel from its own independent phase/offset rather than from a shared spatial wave.

Modes 4 and 12 need the same treatment: both should rest at their baseline (mode 4 G=63, mode 12 B=50) with only occasional flares (original p50 == baseline in both), and both should be about half the port's current brightness (orig meanBrightness 32.2 in each vs port 61.5 / 59.6). Additionally the original's mode 12 has a ~1.8 s cadence (strip-mean autocorr -0.67 at 0.85 s, +0.57 at 1.8 s) that the port's smooth non-repeating swell does not reproduce.

Mode 10 is structurally wrong: the original renders a flat uniform violet across the whole strip (every pixel 100,0,255, with a 99/100 dither), while the port renders a 5-pixel repeating cycle [0,71,255] [60,0,255] [255,0,235] [255,0,235] [60,0,255]. Make mode 10 a uniform 100,0,255.

Static-mode colour corrections (exact target RGB, uniform across the strip): mode 1 should be 255,127,35 (port is 255,177,109 — far too pale), mode 2 should be 255,170,98 (port 255,205,166), mode 6 should be 140,255,147 (port 198,255,228), mode 7 should be 255,135,24 (port 255,114,0). The consistent bias is that the port's tinted whites are washed toward neutral — check whichever colour-temperature-to-RGB step is used; modes 3, 5, 8, 9 and 11 are already within a few counts and need no change.

Nothing to fix on timing infrastructure: both sides are already fps-invariant (identical values at the same absolute time at 10/20/40 fps), seed-independent (seeds 1/7/1234 identical), and steady over 240 s with no decay or regime drift. The static modes are exactly static on both sides.
experiments: rwl-sweep-0 .. rwl-sweep-40 (41-point sliderLightType sweep, 0.000..1.000 step 0.025, dumped + hashed to locate every mode boundary on both sides)
